sources.entry: whenever - A modern datetime library, type-safe and DST-safe, in Rust or pure Python.

summary.one_liner: Whenever is a type-safe, DST-safe datetime library for Python with a Rust extension backend and an optional pure-Python backend.
summary.what_it_does: It provides separate types for exact moments (Instant), zoned datetimes (ZonedDateTime) and plain local datetimes (PlainDateTime), so naive and aware values are distinguished by the type system. Arithmetic on zoned values accounts for DST transitions, and a PlainDateTime shifted by exact time units emits a warning. It supports parsing and formatting of ISO 8601, RFC 3339 and RFC 2822, plus custom pattern formatting, rounding and truncation to units such as minutes, and nanosecond precision. Conversion to and from the standard library datetime is available. The README says platform wheels include the Rust extension, while a pure-Python wheel covers other platforms, and PyPy and GraalVM load the pure-Python backend automatically. It is limited to the proleptic Gregorian calendar from years 1 to 9999 and to whole-second UTC offsets.
use_cases: replace naive datetime bugs with typed datetimes
do DST-correct date and time arithmetic
convert times between UTC and named time zones
parse and format ISO 8601 or RFC 3339 timestamps
round or truncate timestamps to a minute or interval
use datetimes with SQLAlchemy or Pydantic models
run datetime code without a compiled Rust extension
notable: Typed split between aware exact instants, zoned datetimes and naive plain datetimes, checkable by typecheckers
DST-safe arithmetic that the README contrasts with the standard library and Arrow/Pendulum
Rust-backed build with a pure-Python fallback for other platforms and PyPy/GraalVM
Nanosecond precision with rounding and custom format patterns
Listed under Date and Time in vinta/awesome-python
caveats: Supports the proleptic Gregorian calendar only between 1 and 9999 AD
Time zone offsets are limited to whole seconds
Free-threading support is labeled beta in the README
